hypothesis: Magnetic analytic-signal ridges (sqrt(tmi_hg^2+tmi_vg^2), coherence-gated on tmi) mark near-vertical basement contacts under cover. The H19-5 skeleton behind R0 is multi-line corroborated, so a contact carried by the magnetic analytic signal alone could be dropped from the skeleton and the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue while still marking a basement fault propagating into basin fill. Placing 45% of the budget on the strongest such ridges >3px off the whole skeleton tests that single-line magnetic channel.
mechanism: At fixed S=37,654, DTI rises when expected T gains outweigh denominator growth. Kept skeleton dots are chosen by exact marginal expected-DTI greedy (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, R=3px) under w=0.30+0.70*S_pct on H19-5 support. Far dots take the strongest analytic-signal ridges first (descending S, 2.8px spacing). In-memory screen (docs/ANALYSIS_20261024_ANASIG.md): f45 hybrid HOLDOUT-DTI 0.004967 vs R0 0.004006, forward overlap 0.528 vs BREAKLINE f45 -- holdout-positive and lane-disjoint, unlike SCARPPOL (0.900 vs BREAKLINE, duplicate-stopped).
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Lithologic contacts without fault offset, dike/sill edges, buried volcanic flow margins, and cultural magnetic noise all produce analytic-signal ridges with no Quaternary fault.
